Frequently.title: What is a public blockchain?
Frequently.desc: A public blockchain is a decentralized network that anyone can join and interact with. All transactions are visible to everyone, and no central authority controls the system.

Frequently.title: How is public blockchain different from private or permissioned blockchains?
Frequently.desc: Public blockchains are open, permissionless, and transparent. Private or permissioned blockchains restrict who can access or validate transactions, making them more suitable for enterprise use.

Frequently.title: What’s an example of a public permissioned blockchain?
Frequently.desc: Ripple (XRP) and Hedera Hashgraph are examples where the network is public, but node participation is permissioned.

Frequently.title: Which is the best public blockchain for development?
Frequently.desc: It depends on your use case. Ethereum is widely adopted, Solana is great for speed, and Polkadot is strong in interoperability.

Frequently.title: How long does it take to develop a public blockchain app?
Frequently.desc: Anywhere from 4 to 20+ weeks, depending on complexity, integrations, and custom features.
